title: Acceptable Misalignment
abstract: arXiv:2610.16881v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: There is a specific challenge designers face in developing autonomous robots capable of open-ended learning. This challenge is how one can develop such systems in an ethically sound way when there are many unknowns during design time about their manner of deployment, what they can and will learn, and how these systems will act on the basis of what they have learned. One response to this challenge is to align, as far as possible, the activities and goals of autonomous robots with human values, raising the question of how to make this alignment possible, a question known as the value alignment problem. We argue that the value alignment problem faces a number of challenges that show that full alignment is both theoretically and practically impossible, meaning that misalignment incidents will keep occurring. translated_abstract: 开发能够进行开放式学习的自主机器人时，设计者面临一个特殊的挑战。这一挑战在于：当在设计阶段对于这些系统的部署方式、它们能够以及将会学到什么、以及它们将如何基于所学内容采取行动存在诸多未知因素时，如何以符合伦理的方式开发这样的系统。针对这一挑战的一种回应是，尽可能地将自主机器人的活动与目标同人类价值观对齐，由此引出了如何实现这种对齐的问题，即所谓的价值对齐问题。我们认为，价值对齐问题面临着诸多挑战，这些挑战表明完全对齐在理论上和实践上都是不可能的，这意味着失调事件将持续发生。这削弱了当前的对齐方法，因为最大化对齐的尝试无法妥善处理相关可能性。（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文论证了对于具备开放式学习能力的自主机器人，完全的价值对齐在理论与实践上均不可能实现，失调事件不可避免，因此应放弃最大化对齐的思路，转而追求“可接受的失调”。
en_tdlr: Full value alignment for autonomous open-ended learning robots is theoretically and practically impossible, making misalignment incidents inevitable; the paper argues for shifting from maximizing alignment toward pursuing "acceptable misalignment."
